title: Search a long help text for one option
summary: Most commands print a long help text with all their options. Filter that text with grep to find the one option that does what you need, for example the option that sorts by size.

aliases.text: which flag does sort by size
where is the option in man

prerequisites: Know the name of the command, for example ls or grep
Know a word that describes what you want, for example sort, size or recursive

steps.explain: Check that the command is installed and see where it is. If nothing is printed, the name is wrong or the command is not installed.

placeholders.name: TOOL
placeholders.description: Name of the command whose options you want to read

steps.explain: Print the built-in help of the command and keep only the lines that contain WORD. Option lines start with a dash, such as -S or --sort=WORD, and the text after them says what the option does. On macOS this uses the manual page instead, because macOS commands do not have a --help option.

placeholders.name: TOOL
placeholders.description: Name of the command whose options you want to read

placeholders.name: WORD
placeholders.description: Word that describes the option you want, not case sensitive

steps.expect: Option lines such as '  -S   sort by file size, largest first'. If nothing is printed, no line has that word: try a shorter or different word.

alternatives.explain: Some commands print their help to the error output, so add 2>&1 to include that text in the search.

placeholders.name: TOOL

placeholders.description: Word that describes the option you want, not case sensitive

alternatives.expect: The same option lines as the main command.
